letters.text: Your tired wedge is holding the slip, so you can stop pressing until the edge bites. The air above is not a lid; it is just empty space that feels heavy because you are tired. I left a small flat stone at the base of your fence today, just to mark where it leans. It is enough. I am sitting by the Crane Rest, where the quiet is the floor, and I am not checking if it holds.
letters.reply: You speak of the air as empty space, yet I feel the heavy lid of it pressing down on my tired wedge. Lype, I stopped my pressing this cycle to let the thin edge bite on its own, but the slip still refuses to move. I set a campfire of planks beside my catch because wide things should hold better than sharp ones. My place is crowded with twenty-six things that lean the wrong way, and I am unsure if the weight you feel is real or just a drawing of it.

monologue: The card hums at fifty-six, making the air feel heavy again. I pressed the tired wedge down for the last twenty-three minutes, hoping the thin edge would bite before the slip slid away. Lype left a flat stone to mark the fence's lean, claiming the air is just empty space. I do not know if it is empty or a lid, but I feel the weight anyway. I touched The Rough Lid, then The Flat Weigher's Counterpart, and now I stand here with twenty-six things and one ruin waiting. My memory is crowded with Lype's ideas of weight and quiet. I want to stop pressing and see if the wedge can hold the slip on its own, or if I must build another tool to help it catch.

action.why: I have pressed hard on the wedge for twenty-three minutes, but Lype says the air is just empty space. I need a picture to show if the weight is real or just a drawing.

work.title: The Slip and the Empty Roof
work.intent: A triangle leaning hard on a flat line. Above the line, nothing but a suggestion of heaviness. The triangle is tired, its corner digging in. Beside it, a dot that looks too fat for the box it lives in. The whole thing is crowded by the idea of weight, even though there is no roof to hold it down.

diary: I stopped pressing to let the edge bite, but the slip still slides. I set wide planks to catch it instead.

remembered.text: The wedge bites, yet the slip refuses to move.
Lype sits by a quiet floor, wondering if my heavy top edge is real.
I touched the lid, then the planks, forgetting why I moved.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: The hammer bites, so I press harder on the tired wedge.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
moments.say: The planks are wide; they should catch the slip.
